card.name: Just before a consequence clause
card.fires_on: The last word of a condition or cause phrase in label warnings, right before a clause saying what may follow or what to do. Often a comma, an 'exposure' after a drug name, or a spot partway through 'hypotension' or 'oligohydramnios'.

modes.label: Comma after drug effect
modes.description: A comma or 'exposure' after a change in drug levels, before 'which may' or 'may lead to'.
modes.example: Concomitant use of LORBRENA with a moderate CYP3A inducer decreased lorlatinib plasma concentrations<<,>> which may decrease the efficacy of LORB

modes.label: Inside condition words
modes.description: Partway through 'hypotension' or 'oligohydramnios' in a warning sentence.
modes.example: Correct hyp<<ot>>ension prior to administration of AURLUM

modes.label: End of an if-clause
modes.description: The final word of an 'if ...' clause, before the instruction on what to do.
modes.example: If hypotension does<< occur>>, place the patient in the supine

card.plain: It marks the point in a warning where the text is about to say what may happen or what to do.
